transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what finally got me to come in is that my work is really taking a hit lately. I'm an electrician, and... I just can't keep my focus on one estimate or code form anymore. 

It's like, I'll sit down to look at the paperwork, and then a tool noise, or a text on my phone, or just some new idea I have about the workshop completely pulls me off track. I end up dropping what I'm doing, and then, you know, my jobs start getting all mixed up. It's becoming a real problem, so I figured I needed to come talk to somebody.
Have you noticed these difficulties with focus and getting distracted in other parts of your life, like at home or with friends, or does it seem to only happen at work?

It's definitely happening at home, too. I mean, at work it's bad enough—clients have actually started complaining about missed details and me mixing up the schedule. Even my apprentices... you can tell they just don't trust my direction the way they used to. 

But at home, yeah, it's a real issue. My wife and I are getting into constant arguments lately, mostly about the mortgage and the business. She feels like I'm putting everything we've built at risk because I just can't keep things straight right now. So it's pretty much affecting everything.
When did you first start noticing these issues with focus and getting distracted? Were they something you experienced even as a child, or did they develop more recently in your life?

No, it's definitely not something from when I was a kid. I was always pretty sharp, you know, good at keeping things organized. This... this is a lot more recent. I'd say it's been building up for about seven months now. That's right around the time my wife and I took on the new mortgage to buy the workshop and all the heavy equipment for the business. Everything just started getting harder to keep track of after that.
Have you found yourself feeling restless, overly energetic, or unable to sit still lately, especially when you're trying to focus on tasks?

Yeah, I definitely have. It's like I just can't stop moving. I've been going nonstop lately—bouncing from job sites to doing bids, and then I'll be in the workshop rewiring test panels. 

I keep starting these new home-automation projects before I even finish the last one I was working on. It just feels like if I sit down or try to stay still, I'm wasting time, you know? I just have this constant need to be doing something.
Have you ever had periods where your mood was extremely high, you felt invincible, or you needed less sleep but still had tons of energy?

Yeah, I definitely have those times. I'll get in this big, pumped-up mood... like, I'll be going on and on about how our little shop is about to become the main solar outfit in town. I just feel completely fired up about it and ready to take on anything. 

But the thing is, if my wife or one of the apprentices questions the plan at all, I can just flip. I end up getting really sharp with them over absolutely nothing. So it's like I'm riding really high, but I get set off super easily.
During these times when you feel really fired up and invincible, have you noticed that you actually need less sleep — like you can go on just fine with only a few hours of rest?

Yeah, exactly that. It's been going on for months now. I'll sleep for maybe three or four hours, and then I just pop right up, way before the sun's even out. And I don't feel tired at all. I wake up feeling completely ready to go—pricing out materials, answering emails, or sketching out another solar system. It feels just like I got a full night's rest, even though I barely slept.
Have you ever noticed that these really high, fired-up periods are followed by times when you feel down, hopeless, or lose interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I can't say I have. I don't really get down or hopeless like that. Honestly, it's mostly just the high energy and being go-go-go all the time. I haven't really noticed any kind of crash or losing interest in my work or anything else.
